title: SCULPFUN Lineup: C1, S9, S30 Pro and E1
metaDescription: SCULPFUN laser engravers compared: the C1 6W mini, S9 5.5W, S30 Pro 10W with air assist and the enclosed dual-laser E1, with area, features and prices from $153 to $937.
author: ByteBuy Team

sections.content: SCULPFUN's range is easiest to read as four steps up: the C1 is a pocket-size starter, the S9 is the proven mid-size diode laser, the S30 Pro adds higher power and automatic air assist, and the E1 is a different design altogether, an enclosed machine with a camera and two lasers. Prices run from $153.41 to $936.98, so the real question is which step matches your projects.

items.label: C1 6W Mini ($153.41)
items.value: 150x130 mm area, 0.06 mm spot, 10,000 mm/min, one-step installation, LightBurn and LaserGRBL compatible

items.label: S9 5.5W ($198.64)
items.value: 410x420 mm area, 0.06 mm compressed spot, fixed focus, listing states 15 mm wood and 10 mm acrylic cutting

items.label: S30 Pro 10W ($499)
items.value: 410x400 mm area expandable to 935x905 mm, automatic air assist, 32-bit board, replaceable lens, 0.06x0.08 mm focus

items.label: E1 12W+3W IR ($936.98)
items.value: Enclosed, 400x320 mm area, 600 mm/s CoreXY, HD camera, Class 1 safety, air assist; the 3W IR laser is a second module alongside the 12W diode

pros: The C1 6W costs only $153.41 and is the easiest to set up, with a one-step installation
The S9 gives a 410x420 mm bed for $198.64, the best area per dollar in the range
The S30 Pro adds automatic air assist, which helps keep cuts clean, and its area can be expanded to 935x905 mm
The E1 is enclosed and lists Class 1 safety, which makes it the most suitable for a home or shared space
The E1's HD camera helps with positioning, and its second IR laser extends what it can mark
cons: The C1's 150x130 mm area limits project size
The S9 is fixed focus and has no air assist built in, so cuts can char more on thick material
The S30 Pro is open-frame, so you need your own eye protection, ventilation and, ideally, an enclosure
The E1 costs more than six times the C1, and its 400x320 mm area is smaller than the S9's
Expanding the S30 Pro to 935x905 mm needs extension parts that the listing does not include; check what is sold separately

items.question: Which SCULPFUN is best for a beginner?
items.answer: The S9 is the all-round starter with a large bed and a low price. The C1 is the cheapest, if your projects are small. Choose the E1 if safety and a closed work area matter more than price.

items.question: Is the S30 Pro worth $300 more than the S9?
items.answer: If you cut regularly, yes: it has about twice the stated power and built-in air assist. For engraving only, the S9 does most of what you need.

items.question: What does the E1's IR laser do?
items.answer: The E1 lists a 12W diode and a 3W infrared module. The listing does not detail materials for the IR laser, so check the product page to see what it is meant to mark.

items.question: Do I need a rotary roller or laser bed?
items.answer: Only for specific jobs: a rotary roller for cylinders such as tumblers and a honeycomb bed for cleaner cuts. SCULPFUN also lists S9 and S30 Pro Max bundles that include them.

items.question: What about the SCULPFUN C1 3W?
items.answer: The catalog also has a 3W C1 at $120.30, with a finer 0.04 mm spot. It is the same mini format with lower power.

sections.content: Match the step to the work: the C1 for small marking, the S9 for a large bed on a budget, the S30 Pro for regular cutting, and the E1 when you want an enclosed, camera-guided machine. Whichever you pick, plan for eye protection and ventilation.
